findings.statement: CA9 transcripts sit in the RCC tumour cell group [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976], and a large fraction of RCC cells express it [gene=CA9; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; tissue=tumor; groups.0.pct_expressing=54.7%], so the bulk signal is tumour-intrinsic. Tumour cells are far above proximal tubule cells when paired by donor [gene=CA9; type=sc_tumor_vs_pt; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; log2fc=7.739].

In Visium, the composition-corrected expresser of CA9 is RCC, and high-CA9 spots are surrounded by RCC spots more often than expected [gene=CA9; type=spatial_neighborhood; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=RCC; log2_enrichment=0.381] [gene=CA9; type=spatial_neighborhood; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=RCC; padj=0.0017]. Macrophage enrichment is small by comparison.

The AlphaFold model of CA9 is of moderate confidence [gene=CA9; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=76.56]. Its top cavity gives a moderate structural-context score [gene=CA9; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; structural_context_score=0.546], and the detected cavities recover part of the experimental ligand contacts [gene=CA9; type=ligand_site_validation; source=PDBe-KB ligand sites (experimental holo structures); recall=0.5]. This is a descriptive monomer heuristic, not a prediction of a degron or of degradability.

KDR is an endothelial gene: endothelial cells carry most of its tumour transcripts [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.951], with a moderate fraction expressing it [gene=KDR; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; tissue=tumor; groups.0.pct_expressing=40.5%]. In situ the composition-corrected expresser is also endothelial, so it is a microenvironment (anti-angiogenic) target, not a tumour-cell target.

CD74 is held by immune cells (macrophages, dendritic cells, B and T cells). Every conventional dendritic cell expresses it [gene=CD74; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=cDC; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=100%] and macrophages hold the largest transcript share, so it is an immune-microenvironment marker, not a tumour-cell target.

CXCR4 is expressed by lymphocytes: most CD4 T cells express it [gene=CXCR4; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=CD4_T; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=87.8%] and CD8 T cells hold the largest transcript share. It is an infiltrating-immune target, not a tumour-cell target.

MET is mostly tumour-cell derived: RCC cells carry most of its tumour transcripts [gene=MET; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.935], with a minority of RCC cells expressing it [gene=MET; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; tissue=tumor; groups.0.pct_expressing=35.2%]. Endothelial cells carry a smaller share.

EPAS1 (HIF-2alpha) transcripts are not tumour-restricted: most endothelial cells express it [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=81.3%] at the highest per-cell level, with fibroblasts also expressing. A bulk EPAS1 signal therefore mixes tumour and stromal sources, although droplet dropout limits this reading.

CD70 is concordantly up in TCGA-KIRC and its purity-extrapolated change persists (tumour-intrinsic), but single-cell attribution is mixed: RCC cells have the highest per-cell level while Treg and CD8 T cells also express it, which matters for ADC or CAR-T targeting. Cell-level numbers have no evidence id, so none are quoted.

COL23A1 (tumour track, first-in-class opportunity) is carried by RCC cells [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881], with few ccRCC papers [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; ccrcc_papers=7] and no clinical drug, and it replicates in TCGA and is purity-robust with no adverse prognosis flag. Missing: a selective DepMap dependency, surface-protein and normal-tissue staining, and tumour-cell heterogeneity, since only a minority of RCC cells express it [gene=COL23A1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; tissue=tumor; groups.0.pct_expressing=17.1%]. The AlphaFold model is low confidence [gene=COL23A1; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=58.91] with a tiny cavity [gene=COL23A1; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; volume_a3=8], so an antibody against an extracellular domain is the more plausible modality.

RAB42 (tumour track) is mainly in RCC cells [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627], has very few ccRCC papers [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; ccrcc_papers=2] and no clinical drug, replicates in TCGA and is purity-robust. It is an intracellular GTPase, so antibody tractability is doubtful; no dependency or functional evidence exists, and literature is counted by gene symbol.

OLFML2A (stroma track) is a fibroblast gene [gene=OLFML2A; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Fibroblast; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.647], expressed by a minority of fibroblasts [gene=OLFML2A; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; tissue=tumor; groups.0.pct_expressing=38.3%], with very few ccRCC papers [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; ccrcc_papers=2], no clinical drug and antibody tractability; it replicates in TCGA and is purity-robust. Caveats: vital-organ expression in colon [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; vital_max_ntpm=27.9], no dependency evidence, and a fibroblast target would act on the microenvironment.

JAG2 (stroma track) is partly endothelial [gene=JAG2; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.487], with few ccRCC papers [gene=JAG2; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; ccrcc_papers=9], no clinical drug and antibody tractability; it replicates in TCGA and is purity-robust. The effect size is modest and it is expressed in heart muscle [gene=JAG2; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; vital_max_ntpm=12.7], so off-tumour risk and absent dependency evidence limit it.

GAL3ST4 (immune track) is a macrophage gene [gene=GAL3ST4; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Macrophage; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.972], expressed by a minority of macrophages [gene=GAL3ST4; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; tissue=tumor; groups.0.pct_expressing=23.7%], with a single ccRCC paper [gene=GAL3ST4; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; ccrcc_papers=1] and no clinical drug; it replicates in TCGA and TCGA survival flags adverse prognosis. Its bulk rise shrinks strongly at full purity [gene=GAL3ST4; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.401], so the bulk signal is largely a macrophage-abundance readout. Missing: function in macrophages, surface expression and dependency.

LILRB4 (immune track) is macrophage-derived [gene=LILRB4; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; source_share=0.933] and is flagged infiltration-driven and not purity-robust [gene=LILRB4; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.508], so its bulk increase largely reflects immune infiltration. It is an immune-checkpoint-type hypothesis with few ccRCC papers [gene=LILRB4; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; ccrcc_papers=7] and no clinical drug here, and needs functional validation.

caveats: Convergence ranking top genes (ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD, FABP1, NPHS2, PIGR) are tumour-down proximal-tubule genes, so they are biomarkers of loss of the normal epithelium, not therapeutic targets; they were not profiled at cell level here.
Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses; none has dependency or functional evidence and literature is counted by gene symbol.
The structural-context score is a monomer cavity heuristic; it does not identify degrons, ligase compatibility or degradation.
Single-cell data cover 12 donors, and some cell groups (PT, Epi_other) have very few cells; EGFR was not profiled within the call budget; CD70 cell-level records carry no evidence id.
